thread:
Mira: Heads-up — canary cluster 3 after last runtime roll (kernel-redispatch + quant v2) shows prefix cache hitrate drop ~28% on production trace. Rolling back now?
Alex: ouch. Which metric exactly — early-token hit or overall?
Mira: early-token (first 8 tokens) hit rate went from ~72% -> ~52% on these traces, tail latencies up ~18ms P95. overall token hit down ~13%.
Jon: any change in key canonicalization? We changed a little salt in key generation with the new kernel, right?
Mira: we didn't change canonicalization explicitly, but the kernel now force-pads nulls to 8-byte boundaries for matmul alignment. suspect key bytes differ.
Pei: can you paste sample keys + compare? also which model variant and quant profile?
Mira: model: redwood-open-13b-quantv2, kernel: fused-attn-redispatch-2024-10, scheduler: batch-adaptive-v3. Sample (hex prefixes):
```
old_key: 3f8a1b2c5d00e1f4a7c...
new_key: 3f8a1b2c5d80e1f4a7c...
```
Mira: see the extra 0x80 byte at offset 6 for many keys. Looks like padding bit flipped.
Sophia: @Mira can you run quick diff of tokenizer-normalized prefixes? maybe tokenizer output changed due to v2 quant tokenization map?
Mira: running now — small script: `python tools/pfx_diff.py --trace canary3 --cmp old new` returns ~6% of prefixes show trailing null bytes inserted.
Jon: that matches padding theory. Why would kernel change append a byte to the serialized KV key? Kernel shouldn't touch serialized cache keys. Is serialization done in runtime before kernel handoff?
Alex: yes, key serialization happens in runtime layer, but we pass raw tensors to kernel; kernel may be returning different dtype/layout triggering different serialization code path (we added a layout check that toggles a fast path that pads).
Pei: can we reproduce locally with the new kernel and a small trace? I'd like a minimized repro.
Mira: repro attached: `run_repro --model redwood-open-13b-quantv2 --trace sample_prompt_0421` gave same key shift.
deploy-bot: deploy event: kernel=fused-attn-redispatch-2024-10 started canary rollout at 2024-10-12T15:40:02Z
Alex: hypothesis: layout fast-path sets `pad_align=true` and serialization code does `memcpy` up to aligned length -> extra zero byte in buffer. Cache lookup uses raw bytes -> miss.
Sophia: quick mitigation: canonicalize keys by trimming trailing 0x00 during lookup until we fix upstream? cheap and safe?
Jon: trimming could mask other bugs but is low-risk in canary. Need to check for legitimate trailing zeros for some model tokens — unlikely.
Pei: risks: trimming changes key space and could cause accidental hits mixing different physical prefixes. But for null padding it's okay. We should add a flag gated by runtime param `strip_zero_suffix_for_canary=true`.
Mira: patched runtime locally: added `if (strip_zero_suffix) while (key.len>0 && key.back()==0) key.pop_back();` quick test: hitrate returns to 71% on repro.
Alex: nice. Put a canary flag and roll. Also add a metric to count how many keys had zeros stripped to measure scope.
Sophia: also add unit test for serializer path with pad_align true/false.
Jon: long-term we should ensure kernel never influences serialized representation. File a follow-up with kernel team to remove layout side-effect or explicitly return canonical bytes.
Mira: opened ticket: KERNEL-1428 with logs and repro. assigned to kernel-team (pinged @kernel-owners).
Pei: did the change also affect K/V eviction patterns? if keys differ we'll create many cold entries and evictions -> cost bump.
Mira: yes canary memory churn + higher misses observed. Eviction rate up ~23% for canary window.
Alex: rollout plan: 1) enable strip_zero_suffix_for_canary=true in canary clusters 2) add metric `pfx_zero_trim_count` and alarm if > 1% of requests 3) revert kernel if kernel team can't patch in 24h.
Mira: implementing patch and metrics now, will push hotfix.
deploy-bot: staging deploy completed 2024-10-12T16:02:11Z
Sophia: thanks. after hotfix let's run perf comparison: heatmap of early-token hit, eviction rate, P95 latency, cost-per-token. baseline vs canary vs hotfix.
Jon: also add a quick profiler snapshot (alloc + memcpy hotspots) — I suspect serializer memcpy branch is now hot.
Mira: snapshot attached in thread (short). Summary: memcpy count +2.3x on canary vs baseline, heap allocation delta +12MB/min.
Alex: sounds consistent. Good catch. Let's keep thread updated when canary metrics flip. :thumbsup:
